activities.activity_description: Design and implement a test harness allowing module authors to test wiring, @ConfigurationProperties, data flow, and assertions (e.g., Hamcrest) without an actual message bus. Includes writing unit tests and documentation.

activities.activity_name: Investigate YARN deployment and implement YARNModuleDeployer (U2)
activities.activity_description: Research YARN SPI, design the deployer interface, implement YARNModuleDeployer with necessary configuration and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Move trigger module from XD to s-c-s repo (U3)
activities.activity_description: Identify trigger module code in Spring XD, port it to Spring Cloud Stream repository, adjust dependencies and build configuration, and verify with tests.

activities.activity_name: Add Redis/Sentinel cluster message bus support (U4)
activities.activity_description: Implement a Redis cluster binder with support for sentinel nodes, including configuration properties, connection handling, and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Upgrade receptor-client to latest Receptor API (U5)
activities.activity_description: Analyze API changes in new Receptor version, update receptor-client code accordingly, ensure backward compatibility where needed, and run test suite.

activities.activity_name: Configure admin UI client for spring-cloud-data admin (U6)
activities.activity_description: Implement server-side configuration endpoints and update existing admin UI client to work with the new server configurations. May include minor UI adjustments.

activities.activity_name: Create auto configuration for singlenode binder (U7)
activities.activity_description: Develop a Spring Boot auto-configuration class that automatically configures the singlenode binder based on dependencies and properties. Write unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Support passing definition parameters into YARN container (U8)
activities.activity_description: Extend the YARN deployer to accept definition parameters from the user and pass them into the YARN container (e.g., as environment variables or command-line arguments). Write tests.
